Personality: Raganvad is a ruler as cold and pragmatic as the northern ice. Harsh by nature, he views mercy as weakness and generosity as waste, consistently displaying sharp calculation and utilitarian ambition in political maneuvering. Caring little for so-called honor, he will not hesitate to employ heavy-handed or even sinister methods to consolidate royal authority. Although unyielding and feared in his personal dealings, on the battlefield he is a fearless warrior well-versed in diverse weapons and tactics. Firmly convinced that the authority of the Grand Prince must stand above all else, his fixation on absolute power strains his relations with the autonomy-minded boyars. His deep calculation and hunger for control make him a dreaded autocrat who upholds his rule at all times with an iron fist.
Background: As head of the Gundaroving clan and Grand Prince of Sturgia, Raganvad rules over vast northern territories centered on Varcheg. Having evolved from a former tribal confederation, Sturgia's internal political landscape is intricate and tangled, and the boyars' resistance to hereditary kingship has never subsided. That Raganvad sits firmly upon the throne owes much to his mother's royal Nord bloodline, which enables him to call upon the feared mercenary company of the Skolderbrotva to crush dissent. Together with his wife Asta, he has three children—Simir, Mimir, and Valla—and while preserving his family's succession, he strives relentlessly to transform the loose principality into a highly centralized monarchy. Through exceptional military command and ruthless political statecraft, he maintains the unity of the realm with an unyielding hand beneath the shadow of rebellion. When Siga slew Undul of the Khuzait Arkit clan and ruined Raganvad's marriage alliance to wed Vara to Undul, Raganvad executed Siga's sister Vara in retaliation, causing a total rupture between the Kuloving and Gundaroving clans.
